findings.evidence: TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Ideal/DegreeOne.lean:107 `theorem absNorm_span_natCast_of_finrank_eq_one (hK : Module.finrank ℚ K = 1) (n : ℕ) : Ideal.absNorm (Ideal.span {(n : 𝓞 K)}) = n := by rw [Ideal.absNorm_span_natCast, RingOfIntegers.rank, hK, pow_one]`
findings.fix: In both places, use `RingOfIntegers.absNorm_span_natCast_of_finrank_eq_one (Module.finrank_self ℚ)` instead of the four-step rewrite.
findings.issue: The rewrite chain `Ideal.absNorm_span_natCast, RingOfIntegers.rank, Module.finrank_self, pow_one` repeats the proof of an existing Tau Ceti lemma. The same chain appears again at line 201 in `normCoeff_toPrimitiveRayClassCharacter`.

findings.evidence: grep: lines 54, 76 and 109 each contain `⟨Ideal.absNorm_eq_zero_iff.not.mpr η.conductor.finitePart_ne_bot⟩`.
findings.fix: Define it once as a private lemma or instance about `PrimitiveRayClassCharacter ℚ`, and use that in all three places.
findings.issue: The instance `NeZero (Ideal.absNorm η.conductor.finitePart)` is built by hand three times: in `backward` (line 54), in `hright` (line 76) and in `toPrimitiveRayClassCharacter_symm_apply` (line 109).

findings.evidence: Lines 162–171 move between `Ideal.isCoprime_span_singleton_iff`, `Nat.isCoprime_iff_coprime` and `Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv` maps, and nothing in that argument depends on ψ. A grep of NumberField/{Rat,IntegersRat,Dirichlet}*.lean found no existing lemma of this form.
findings.fix: State it as its own lemma about `ratModulus` (for example, next to `Rat.RingOfIntegers.ideal_span_absNorm_eq_self`) and call it here.
findings.issue: The ideal-weight proof contains a ten-line `hcop` block proving that `(ratModulus n).IsCoprimeTo J ↔ (Ideal.absNorm J).Coprime n` for nonzero `J`. This is a general fact about ideals of `𝓞 ℚ`, but it is only available inside this proof.

summary: The proofs are readable and contain no undocumented definitional-equality tricks, but they repeat the proof of an existing degree-one norm lemma, build the same NeZero instance three times, and hide a reusable coprimality fact inside the ideal-weight proof.
